title: Formatting of InputEventKey is confusing/misleading
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.5.1, 4.3, probably most other 4.X versions

### System information

N/A

### Issue description

The way that `InputEventKey` is formatted when printed is quite confusing and doesn't represent the actual contents of `InputEventKey` very well.

Some examples:
```gdscript
var event_all := InputEventKey.new()
event_all.keycode = KEY_W
event_all.physical_keycode = KEY_W
event_all.unicode = ord('w')
print(event_all)

var event_k := InputEventKey.new()
event_k.keycode = KEY_W
print(event_k)

var event_pk := InputEventKey.new()
event_pk.physical_keycode = KEY_W
print(event_pk)

var event_u := InputEventKey.new()
event_u.unicode = ord('w')
print(event_u)
```

This produces the following:
```text
InputEventKey: keycode=87 (W), mods=none, physical=false, location=unspecified, pressed=false, echo=false
InputEventKey: keycode=87 (W), mods=none, physical=false, location=unspecified, pressed=false, echo=false
InputEventKey: keycode=87 (W), mods=none, physical=true, location=unspecified, pressed=false, echo=false
InputEventKey: keycode=U+77 (w), mods=none, physical=false, location=unspecified, pressed=false, echo=false
```

There are at least three things here that I find confusing and misleading:
* The first two events produce the exact same output, despite clearly not being equal.
* The value labeled `keycode` can correspond to either `keycode`, `physical_keycode` or `unicode` field, depending on which of these fields are set.
* There is a value labeled `physical`, despite the fact that `InputEventKey` has no such field.

I think it would be much clearer to just print the actual fields of `InputEventKey`.
